key_insight: Coarse-mesh graph neural networks predict sparse flow observables without reconstructing the full state, matching or outperforming finer-mesh surrogates at lower cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces training time and memory for predicting selected flow measurements and integrated quantities, supporting system identification and state estimation from sparse observations.
method: Train parameterized GNN surrogates directly on coarse flow meshes.
Select training parameters adaptively using changes in frequency spectra.
Use noise-augmented multi-step unrolling to improve long-horizon autoregressive predictions.
evidence_signal: Tests on parameterized 2D/3D confined cylinder flows and an unevenly heated cavity showed generalization to unseen conditions; adaptive sampling reduced maximum errors by an order of magnitude versus uniform sampling.
watch_item: Validation covers selected flow configurations and parameter ranges; performance on new geometries or substantially different regimes remains to be established.
paper_title: Predicting Sparse Observables in Parameterized Unsteady Flows Using Coarse-Mesh Graph Neural Networks
